options: To make addresses shorter than IPv4
IPv4's roughly 4.3 billion addresses were exhausted; IPv6's 128-bit space provides a vastly larger pool
Because IPv4 cannot be routed over the internet
questions.explain: IPv4's 32-bit space (about 4.3 billion addresses) was exhausted at the regional registry level; IPv6's 128-bit space provides roughly 340 undecillion addresses.

questions.q: How many times can the "::" shorthand be used in a single IPv6 address?
questions.explain: "::" can only appear once per address, because using it twice would make it impossible to determine how many zero groups each instance represents.

questions.q: What prefix do all IPv6 link-local addresses start with?
questions.explain: Link-local addresses always start with fe80::/10 — automatically self-assigned on every IPv6-enabled interface, valid only on the local segment.

questions.q: What does IPv6 use instead of IPv4's broadcast address?
options: IPv6 still uses broadcast, identical to IPv4
Multicast, sent only to the specific group of interfaces that need it
IPv6 has no equivalent mechanism at all
Unicast to every address on the subnet individually
questions.explain: IPv6 has no broadcast address at all — functions IPv4 handled with broadcast, like ARP-equivalent neighbor discovery, use multicast instead, delivered only to the relevant group.

questions.q: Why does an IPv4-only firewall rule set create a real security risk on a modern network?
options: It doesn't — IPv6 is never enabled by default anywhere
Modern OSes often run IPv6 by default alongside IPv4, so IPv4-only controls can leave an entire IPv6 path completely unmonitored
IPv6 cannot carry malicious traffic by design
Firewalls are incapable of filtering IPv6 under any circumstances
questions.explain: IPv6 is frequently enabled by default even on networks that don't intentionally use it, so security controls scoped only to IPv4 can leave a real, unmonitored attack surface on the IPv6 stack.
